Based on `docs/adr/0000-podzial-na-moduly-domenowe.md` and the existing `retail-operations-portal/.oxlintrc.json` setup, lint (`no-restricted-imports`) only stops *deep imports*. It does **not** stop someone from weakening the rule itself, widening a module's public API to "launder" access, or dumping things into `shared`/`platform` as an escape hatch. Those need separate defenses:

## What's already enforced (tooling)
- Deep imports (`@/modules/x/internal/...`) and relative `../modules/...` imports → blocked by `no-restricted-imports` in root + per-module `.oxlintrc.json`.

## Gaps and how to close them

| Bypass tactic | Why lint alone doesn't stop it | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Delete/downgrade the rule (`error`→`warn`), or remove `extends` in a module's config | Anyone can edit `.oxlintrc.json` in a normal PR; nested configs don't auto-merge (child must restate the rule) | Require **CI** to run `npm run lint` and fail the build; add **CODEOWNERS** on the root and all 4 module `.oxlintrc.json` files requiring architecture/tech-lead approval to touch them |
| Inline `oxlint-disable(-next-line) no-restricted-imports` comment | Lint config itself doesn't need to change | Add a CI grep step that fails if that disable directive appears in diffed files (or a periodic repo-wide check) |
| "Laundering" — the *owning* team adds an export to their own `index.ts` just to satisfy an external caller, widening the public API beyond what's warranted | Lint permits any file to import its own module's internals, so this isn't a lint violation | CODEOWNERS on each module's `index.ts`, requiring the owning team's sign-off; convention that new public exports need a one-line justification/ADR link in the PR |
| Dumping a type/util into `shared`/`platform` to dodge the boundary entirely | `shared`/`platform` is legitimately importable by everyone, so it's invisible to lint | CODEOWNERS on `shared/` and `platform/`; the ADR already flags the old flat `types.ts` as the anti-pattern to avoid repeating — treat any *new* addition to shared as requiring review, not just any dependency-direction issue |
| Direct push / merge without review, bypassing all of the above | No CI or CODEOWNERS currently exist in this repo | Enable branch protection on the default branch: required status check = lint/build, required PR review from CODEOWNERS |

No `.github/workflows`, `CODEOWNERS`, or branch protection exist in this repo yet — the checks above are the actual missing enforcement layer, not the import rule itself.

**Before I scaffold CI + CODEOWNERS**, I need real GitHub identities to map to the ownership map in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (Catalog Team, Pricing Team, Sales & Fulfillment Team, Platform Team) — what are the GitHub usernames/teams for each? And is this hosted on GitHub (CODEOWNERS + branch protection) or another platform (GitLab has equivalent CODEOWNERS + protected branches)?

_**Agent (copilot/claude-sonnet-5)**_

`no-restricted-imports` only sees `import`/`export ... from` edges. A `declare global { ... }` block (or an ambient `.d.ts` with no top-level import/export) injects symbols into global scope with **zero import statement anywhere** — completely invisible to that rule, to dependency-cruiser, to `eslint-plugin-boundaries`, to anything that walks the module graph. It's the same anti-pattern the ADR already flagged for the old flat `types.ts`, just made worse because it's undetectable by graph tooling.

Two things currently help a little but don't close the gap:
- `tsconfig.app.json` sets `moduleDetection: "force"`, so a plain `.ts`/`.tsx` file without imports/exports is still treated as a module scope, not auto-global.
- But `declare global {...}` is the explicit escape hatch that overrides that — it still works inside a module file, and a genuinely ambient `.d.ts` (no top-level import/export) is global regardless.

There's no lint rule for this yet (repo has zero `declare global`/`.d.ts` files today — clean slate). I added a small dependency-free guard script that fails if anyone introduces one inside `src/modules/**`:

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Fails if any module file declares ambient globals, which bypass no-restricted-imports
// (no import statement exists, so the module boundary lint rule can't see the dependency).
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join } from "node:path";

const MODULES_ROOT = join(import.meta.dirname, "..", "src", "modules");
const FORBIDDEN = /\bdeclare\s+global\b/;
const offenders = [];

function walk(dir) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const full = join(dir, entry);
    if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) {
      walk(full);
      continue;
    }
    if (![".ts", ".tsx"].includes(extname(entry))) continue;
    if (FORBIDDEN.test(readFileSync(full, "utf8"))) offenders.push(full);
  }
}

walk(MODULES_ROOT);

if (offenders.length > 0) {
  console.error(
    "`declare global` is forbidden inside src/modules/** — it makes symbols globally " +
      "visible without an import, bypassing the no-restricted-imports module boundary rule.\n" +
      "Offending files:"
  );
  for (const f of offenders) console.error(`  - ${f}`);
  process.exit(1);
}

```

    "`declare global` is forbidden inside src/modules/** — it makes symbols globally " +
      "visible without an import, bypassing the no-restricted-imports module boundary rule.\n" +
      "Offending files:"
  );
  for (const f of offenders) console.error(`  - ${f}`);
  process.exit(1);
}

```
